subject: Computer Networking
title: SolarWinds Supply Chain Attack (2020)
description: A 60-second lesson on SolarWinds Supply Chain Attack (2020).

hook.text: Hackers hid inside a trusted software update. 18,000 orgs installed it, including U.S. government agencies.

buildup.text: SolarWinds Orion, a monitoring tool, was compromised. Attackers injected a backdoor into its build system.

discovery.text: Every org that updated Orion installed the backdoor. Attackers had access for months before discovery.

twist.text: FireEye found it only because the hackers stole FireEye's own tools. A security firm hacked by its own find.

climax.text: The breach hit the Pentagon, Treasury, and Homeland Security. Attributed to Russian intelligence.

punchline.text: The most trusted update became the most dangerous backdoor.

quiz.question: What made the SolarWinds attack so effective?
options: The backdoor was hidden inside a legitimate, trusted software update
It exploited a zero-day in all web browsers
It used brute force to crack passwords at scale

details.summary: In 2020, Russian hackers compromised SolarWinds' Orion software build process and inserted a backdoor into updates sent to 18,000 organizations, including US government agencies and Fortune 500 companies. The attackers had months of undetected access to some of the world's most sensitive networks.
details.whyItMatters: SolarWinds demonstrated that supply chain attacks can compromise thousands of organizations through a single trusted software vendor, undermining the entire software trust model.
takeaways: Hackers compromised the software build process itself
The attack went undetected for months across government agencies

faq.question: How did attackers compromise SolarWinds undetected?
faq.answer: They infiltrated SolarWinds' build system and injected malicious code into the Orion software update. The backdoor was digitally signed with SolarWinds' legitimate certificate, so security tools trusted it. The attackers then selectively activated access in high-value targets.

faq.question: What made the SolarWinds attack so significant?
faq.answer: It compromised the software supply chain, meaning organizations were infected by trusting their own vendor's updates. Victims included the US Treasury, Commerce Department, and major tech companies. It forced a fundamental rethinking of software supply chain security.
